title: Monitoring protein synthesis by fluorescence recovery after photobleaching \(FRAP) _in vivo_
protocol: Grow transgenic animals expressing the fluorophore on 60mm plates seeded with OP50.
Maintain animals at a standard temperature of 20°C or an appropriate alternative based on genetic background and experimental requirements.
Allow animals to equilibrate at the temperature for 2-3 hours before photobleaching.
Perform the procedure directly on a plate (method A).
Transfer single worms to fresh 35mm plates seeded with OP50 bacteria.
Place a small bacterial spot at the center of each plate for easy localization of the worm.
Spot a drop of 15 μl M9 buffer on a microscope slide.
Place the worm on the drop using an eyelash glued to a pick.
Add a cover slip over the drop containing the worm.
Photograph single animals before photobleaching using a camera attached to the microscope.
Document imaging parameters such as lens, magnifier used, filters, exposure time, and resolution.
Perform photobleaching using an epifluorescence compound light microscope equipped with a high power light source and appropriate excitation/emission filter sets.
Use a mercury arc lamp for the light source.
Adjust the light intensity and duration of photobleaching to reduce initial emission intensity to within 10-30% of pre-bleach levels.
Photograph each animal immediately after photobleaching, collecting several images of cells or tissues of interest.
Move animals to fresh OP50-seeded NGM plates.
Follow fluorescence recovery by photographing animals at defined time points, using one-hour intervals between photography sessions.
Collect several images of cells or tissues of interest during follow-up imaging.
Ensure all imaging parameters remain identical to those initially set.
Prepare a stock solution of cycloheximide by diluting in water to a concentration of 10 mg/ml.
Keep the cycloheximide stock refrigerated.
Add cycloheximide on top of OP50-seeded, 35 mm NGM plates to achieve a final concentration of 500 μg/ml in the agar volume.
Allow the plates to dry completely.
Transfer animals onto cycloheximide-containing plates.
Incubate the transferred animals for 2 hours at the growth temperature.
Prepare animals for photobleaching as described in step 2 (A) or (B).
Return worms to cycloheximide-containing plates during fluorescence recovery.
Process images acquired in steps 3, 5, and 6 with ImageJ.
Set pixel depth to 8 bit (256 shades of grey) for each image.
Use the "freehand selection" tool to enclose the fluorescent area of interest.
Select the "measurement" command via the "analyze" drop-down menu.
Adjust threshold until the region of interest is marked using the "threshold" command under the "image" drop-down menu.
Select the "analyze particles" command from the "analyze" drop-down menu.
Check whether measurements correspond to the area of interest by selecting "outlines" at the "show" drop-down menu.
